# SocialCrawl API Overview

## Base URL

```
https://www.socialcrawl.dev
```

## Authentication

Pass your API key in the `x-api-key` header with every request:

```bash
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/profile?handle=charlidamelio"
```

## Surface

<!-- BEGIN:GENERATED:SURFACE (auto-generated by generate-docs.ts - AIP-16b) -->
**65 platforms, 572 active endpoints** (31 of them social). Most are `GET /v1/{platform}/{resource}`, but not all: the batch read endpoints take a JSON body over POST, and the stateful `/v1/web/*` job, monitor, and session routes use POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE. Three surfaces sit on top of the registry: the cross-platform **Prism** composites (`/v1/prism/*` and per-platform `profile/full` / `omni-search`), the stateful **Monitors** family (`/v1/monitors/*`), and the stateful **Cohorts** family (`/v1/cohorts/*` + `/v1/cohort-queries/*`) - neither stateful family is counted in the 572. One more call fans out across 17 sources at once: `/v1/search/everywhere`. See [prism.md](prism.md), [monitors.md](monitors.md), [cohorts.md](cohorts.md), and [search.md](search.md).
<!-- END:GENERATED:SURFACE -->

## Response Format

All successful responses follow this envelope:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "platform": "tiktok",
  "endpoint": "/v1/tiktok/profile",
  "data": { ... },
  "credits_used": 1,
  "credits_remaining": 4999,
  "request_id": "req-XXXXX",
  "cached": false
}
```

Every **list** response also carries a top-level `pagination` block alongside `data`:

```json
"pagination": { "next_cursor": "sc.eyJ...", "has_more": true, "page_size": 30 }
```

`has_more` is the explicit stop signal. Prefer it over inspecting `data.next_cursor` (retained for backwards compatibility) or `total` (which can be estimated or absent).

`credits_remaining` is `integer | null`. It is authoritative on a **billed** response, where it comes straight from the deduction. Every free response-cache hit deliberately skips a blocking balance read, so its body value is `null` and `X-Credits-Remaining` is omitted. An idempotency replay also uses that unknown representation if its current-balance lookup fails. **`null` means unknown; it is never a fabricated zero**, so a `0` here really does mean the account is empty. Poll `GET /v1/credits/balance` when you need a guaranteed reading, and gate any pause-or-alert logic on `!== null && === 0` rather than on falsiness.

Error responses:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS",
    "message": "Your account has 0 credits remaining. This endpoint requires 1 credits.",
    "status": 402,
    "doc_url": "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/docs/errors/insufficient-credits"
  },
  "credits_remaining": 0,
  "request_id": "req-XXXXX"
}
```

## Response Headers

| Header | Value |
|--------|-------|
| X-Request-Id | Unique request identifier (`req-XXXXX`) |
| X-Credits-Used | Credits consumed by this request (`0` on cache hit, idempotent replay, or refunded error) |
| X-Credits-Remaining | Balance after deduction |
| X-Cache | `HIT` or `MISS` |
| X-Idempotent-Replay | `"true"` when the request was served as an idempotent replay. Absent otherwise. |
| X-RateLimit-Limit / -Remaining / -Reset | Request-window budget (600/min per key). Omitted when the limiter is degraded |
| Retry-After | Seconds to wait, on 503 circuit-breaker (`"30"`), 429 `RATE_LIMITED`, and 429 `CONCURRENCY_LIMIT` responses |
| Allow | The method(s) the endpoint actually accepts, only on 405 `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` responses. Not always `GET`: the batch and `/v1/web/*` routes accept POST/PATCH/DELETE |

Counted by underlying tier (custom endpoints folded into their base tier), the split is **327 standard - 210 advanced - 35 premium = 572**. Per-endpoint costs, cache TTLs, and the full rule behind every metered endpoint: see [pricing.md](pricing.md).

Every account starts with **100 free credits**. Credit packs (one-time, no subscription): Starter 2,500 (£15), Growth 20,000 (£49), Pro 150,000 (£299), Enterprise custom. Current packs at https://socialcrawl.dev/pricing.

**Auto-refunds.** Credits are refunded automatically on `502 UPSTREAM_ERROR`, `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, and `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` from the empty-upstream guard. You only pay for calls that return real data.

## Credit Balance

Check remaining credits via the public, API-key-authed meta endpoint (costs **0 credits**, never cached):

```bash
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/credits/balance"
```

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "platform": "meta",
  "endpoint": "/v1/credits/balance",
  "data": {
    "balance": 8432,
    "recent_deductions": { "last_24h": 128, "last_7d": 1043 }
  },
  "credits_used": 0,
  "credits_remaining": 8432,
  "request_id": "req-XXXXX",
  "cached": false
}
```

The dashboard UI uses a separate session-authed `/api/credits/balance` route. Programmatic callers must use `/v1/credits/balance`.

For a full credit ledger (dispute-grade receipts. Deductions negative, refunds positive, newest first), call `GET /v1/credits/transactions` (also **0 credits**, never cached). It is cursor-paginated (`limit` defaults to 50, capped at 100) and filterable by `request_id`:

```bash
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/credits/transactions?limit=50"
```

## Unified Canonical Schemas

Author, Post, and Comment endpoints are normalized through per-platform field maps into one canonical shape, validated at the wire, the same JSON structure whether the data came from TikTok, Reddit, or Bluesky.

**Author** (`data.author`): `id`, `username`, `display_name`, `avatar_url`, `bio`, `verified`, `followers`, `following`, `posts_count`, `likes_count`, `url`, `location`, `external_url`. IDs are bare and prefix-stripped (Bluesky `did:`, Spotify `spotify:artist:`, Reddit `t2_` all stripped).

**Post** (`data.post`, or `data.items[].post` in lists): `id`, `url`, `content.{text, media_urls, thumbnail_url, duration_seconds}`, `author.{username, display_name, avatar_url, verified}`, `engagement.{views, likes, comments, shares, saves}`, `flags.{nsfw, spoiler, pinned, deleted}`, `published_at`. `media_urls` is an array for carousels. `flags.deleted` is always present.

**Comment** (`data.comment`, or `data.items[].comment` in lists): `id`, `url`, `parent_id`, `post_id`, `text`, `author.{username, display_name, avatar_url, verified}`, `engagement.{likes, replies}`, `flags.{pinned, deleted}`, `published_at`. Deleted/removed sentinels (`[deleted]`, `[removed]`) never reach `text`/`author`. They become `null` and `flags.deleted` flips `true`.

**Post and Comment are different archetypes, deliberately.** A post's body is `post.content.text` and its reply count is `post.engagement.comments`; a comment's body is `comment.text` and its reply count is `comment.engagement.replies`. So `/v1/twitter/search/tweets` returns `post.content.text` while `/v1/twitter/tweet/replies` returns `comment.text`, on the same platform, by design: a comment has no media block, no thumbnail and no duration, so it does not carry a `content` wrapper, and "comments on a post" and "replies to a comment" are different quantities that must not share a name. The archetype is named on every endpoint's `**Returns**` line, so read that rather than assuming one shape per platform. The search lanes (`/v1/search/*`) are a third thing again: their `top_comments[]` rows are a search-enrichment structure (`{ score, excerpt, truncated, author, url, date }`), not the Comment archetype, and their body field is `excerpt`.

**Commerce, places & apps archetypes** (the commerce, review, place and app-store platforms):

- **Product**: Amazon, Walmart, Target, eBay, Home Depot, Google Shopping (title, price, rating, brand, images, specifications, variant ids). One shape across all six, so a cross-retailer comparison needs no per-retailer mapping.
- **Review**: shared across Amazon, Walmart, Target, Home Depot, Google Shopping, Trustpilot, Tripadvisor, Google Business, Google Play, Apple App Store (`id`, `title`, `text`, `author`, `rating`, `helpful_votes`, `published_at`, `source`, `responses[]` for owner/developer replies, `images`).
- **Seller**: Amazon, Walmart, Google Shopping per-seller offers (name, price, condition, rating).
- **Place**: Tripadvisor, Google Business (name, category, rating, reviews_count, price_level, phone, latitude/longitude, image_urls; Google hotel results add a `place.hotel` block with amenities, sentiment topics, and multi-vendor prices).
- **App**: Google Play + Apple App Store share one App object with a `store` discriminator (`"google_play"` / `"app_store"`); store-exclusive fields (`installs`/`genres` on Google, `languages`/`advisories` on Apple) are null on the other store.
- **Job**: the LinkedIn job family (listing, detail, search).
- **Quote**: Google Finance instruments and market movers.
- **NewsArticle**: Google News and the news half of universal search.
- **WebPage**: the `/v1/web/*` scrape / crawl / map / extract surface.
- **Audience** / **Analytics** / **Transcript**: audience breakdowns, composite reports, and caption tracks.

Every endpoint section in a platform reference names its archetype on its `**Returns**` line.

List endpoints return `{ items: [...], next_cursor?, total? }` regardless of the upstream's original key names. Commerce/place/app list items carry no `computed` block.

Research/analytics endpoints (Tavily, Perplexity, Polymarket, Content Analysis aggregates, twitter ai-search) are passthrough. They keep their upstream's native top-level keys.

## Computed Fields

When a field map applies (the Author/Post endpoints, which is most of the social surface), four derived signals are added under `data.computed`:

| Field | Type | Author formula | Post formula |
|-------|------|---------------|-------------|
| `engagement_rate` | `number \| null` | `likes_count / followers` (clamped `[0, 1]`) | `(likes + comments + shares) / views` (clamped `[0, 1]`) |
| `language` | `string \| null` | ISO 639-1 detected from `bio` | ISO 639-1 detected from `post.content.text` |
| `content_category` | `string` | Keyword-based (15 categories) | Keyword-based (15 categories) |
| `estimated_reach` | `number \| null` | `round(followers * engagement_rate * 0.1)` | `round(views * 1.2)` when `views > 0`, else `null` |

`engagement_rate` returns `null` when the divisor or numerator is missing/zero (never `Infinity`, `NaN`, or negatives). Ratios >1.0 are clamped to 1.0 with a `_warnings` entry. Language detection needs ≥10 chars of text, else `null`.

## Integrity: `data.dropped` (list responses)

Every list response carries a `data.dropped` integer, the number of upstream
items discarded because they could not be repaired to the endpoint schema. A
clean page carries `"dropped": 0`, which is a **positive assertion that nothing
was lost**, not a default.

```json
"data": { "items": [ ... ], "total": 42, "dropped": 0 }
```

Read it on every page of a drain. It is the only signal that a page came back
short; `items.length` cannot tell a lossy page from a genuinely small one.

**Placement matters, and it is easy to get wrong.** `dropped` sits inside
`data`, next to `items`, while `pagination` sits at the envelope **root**.
Reading `response.dropped` returns `undefined`, which looks exactly like zero to
a naive check and exactly like an outage to a strict one. Read
`response.data.dropped`.

Singular (non-list) responses carry no `dropped` at all. There is no list to
lose rows from, so its absence there is correct and expected.

## Response Warnings (`data._warnings`)

Successful responses may include an optional `data._warnings: string[]` with non-fatal notices (field-map drift, clamped computed values). **Advisory only**: do not flip success, gate retries, or treat it as an error. Empty arrays are omitted.

## Parameter Validation

Every request is validated **before any credit is deducted**:

1. **Required params**: every required name must be present and non-empty.
2. **`oneOf` groups**: endpoints like `GET /v1/youtube/channel` accept `channelId` / `handle` / `url`; at least one member must be present. Reference files render these as "At least one of `a` / `b` is required."
3. **Optional params**: forwarded to upstream only when provided.
4. **Per-platform format validators**: handles, URLs, subreddits, ASINs (10-char alphanumeric), and URL batches are checked against platform-specific rules at the boundary. Garbage is rejected in <100ms with no charge.

A failing request returns `400 INVALID_REQUEST` with `Missing required parameter(s): ...` or a format message.

## Pagination

List responses use `{ items, next_cursor?, total? }` inside `data`, plus the top-level `pagination` block described above. **Prefer the unified path:** send `pagination.next_cursor` back verbatim as `cursor`, and stop when `has_more` is `false`. The API mints a unified `sc.`-prefixed token (or `sc2.` on a multi-source endpoint, which pins the follow-up page to the provider that served page 1) and translates it into whatever the upstream actually wants.

The native parameter each endpoint uses is still accepted, and is named on that endpoint's `**Pagination**` line in its platform reference. **Most list endpoints paginate** (cursor-based for nearly all platforms; offset-based on Naver):

- **Cursor-based**: pass `next_cursor` back verbatim (don't decode or trim it) in the platform's cursor param, `max_cursor` (TikTok), `continuationToken` (YouTube), `next_max_id` (Instagram, Truth Social), `after` (Reddit), `paginationToken`/`cursor` (LinkedIn), `cursor` (most others). Stop when `next_cursor` is absent.
- **Offset-based** (Naver only): increment `start` yourself (1-indexed, cap 1000) with `display` page size.
- Page size is upstream-decided (10 to 30 items typical). `total` may be exact, estimated, or missing: use `next_cursor` to decide when to stop, not `total`.

## Raw Format

Add `?format=raw` to any endpoint whose response is normalized, to receive the original upstream body instead of the unified schema:

```bash
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/profile?handle=charlidamelio&format=raw"
```

What it changes and what it does not:

- **`data` becomes the upstream body verbatim.** No field map, no computed block, no `_warnings`, no `dropped`, and no envelope `pagination` block, because all four describe the normalized payload. The upstream's own paging fields are in the raw body where the provider put them.
- **The envelope is unchanged.** `success`, `platform`, `endpoint`, `credits_used`, `credits_remaining`, `request_id` and `cached` are all still there, and the price is the same. Raw is a rendering choice, not a discount.
- **It shares the cache with the normalized call.** The response cache stores the raw upstream body and re-transforms on every read, so a raw request can be served from an entry a normalized request filled and vice versa. `format` is deliberately not part of the cache key: one entry, two renderings, no chance of the two disagreeing about what the provider said.
- **The 404-on-empty and refund rules still apply.** A nonexistent handle is still a 404 with the credit returned; raw does not turn an empty result into a 200.
- **It is a no-op where there is nothing to bypass.** Passthrough endpoints (GitHub, Tavily, Polymarket, Perplexity, Naver, Prism, Universal Search, Web, Utility, Content Analysis, twitter ai-search and the other research surfaces) already return the upstream shape, so the parameter changes nothing there.
- **An endpoint that owns the name wins.** A few endpoints take a real `format` parameter of their own (`youtube/transcripts`, `youtube/video/comments`, `youtube/video/comment/replies`, `youtube/video/subtitles`, `google/company/ads`, `utility/llms`, `tavily/extract`, `tavily/crawl`). On those, `format` means what their own docs say and `raw` is rejected by their validator.

## Caching

Responses are cached by deterministic key (platform + resource + sorted query params). Cache category TTLs:

| Category | TTL |
|----------|-----|
| profile | 15 min |
| post | 10 min |
| comments | 5 min |
| search | 2 min |
| analytics | 30 min |

**Cache hits are free**: 0 credits, `X-Cache: HIT`, `cached: true`. If a cached body is empty (resource deleted since), you get `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` at no charge. SSE streaming requests to `/v1/search/everywhere` and `/v1/search/news` skip the cache entirely.

## Idempotent Retries

Any `/v1/*` call can be made safely retryable by sending an `Idempotency-Key` header (UUIDv4 or any opaque 16+ char string):

| Outcome | HTTP | Credits | Notes |
|---------|------|---------|-------|
| First call | (normal) | cost | Reserved before billing; completed response stored for 24h |
| Replay (same key, same params) | 200 with stored body | 0 | `X-Idempotent-Replay: true` |
| Payload mismatch (same key, different params) | 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH` | 0 | Use a fresh key |
| Original request still running | 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` | 0 | Wait for `Retry-After: 1`, then retry the same key |
| Completed body exceeded 64 KB | 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE` | 0 | Use a new key only to make a new billable request |

Keys are scoped per account. An unfinished claim expires after 5 minutes; the claim store fails closed before billing if it is unavailable. Requests without the header skip this subsystem.

GET endpoints cannot combine `Idempotency-Key` with `Accept: text/event-stream`, because an interrupted stream has no complete response body to replay. Use `Accept: application/json` when you need idempotent replay. The unsupported combination returns an unbilled `400 INVALID_REQUEST`; POST batch streams retain their documented replay behavior.

GET endpoints cannot combine `Idempotency-Key` with `Accept: text/event-stream`, because an interrupted stream has no complete response body to replay. Use `Accept: application/json` when you need idempotent replay. The unsupported combination returns an unbilled `400 INVALID_REQUEST`; POST batch streams retain their documented replay behavior.

GET endpoints cannot combine `Idempotency-Key` with `Accept: text/event-stream`, because an interrupted stream has no complete response body to replay. Use `Accept: application/json` when you need idempotent replay. The unsupported combination returns an unbilled `400 INVALID_REQUEST`; POST batch streams retain their documented replay behavior.

## Rate and Concurrency Limits

Two separate limits, both per API key, both unbilled when they trip:

| Limit | Value | Code | Headers |
|-------|-------|------|---------|
| Requests per window | 600 per minute (sliding) | `429 RATE_LIMITED` | `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset`, `Retry-After` |
| Simultaneous in-flight | 50 concurrent | `429 CONCURRENCY_LIMIT` | `Retry-After` |

Honor `Retry-After`, then back off exponentially with jitter. The request-window limiter fails open, so a limiter outage never blocks traffic.

A JSON request body over **1 MB** is rejected with `413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` before it is parsed. Split an oversized batch instead.

## Task-Polled Platforms (latency note)

Google Shopping, Trustpilot, Tripadvisor, Google Trends, Google Finance, Content Analysis, most Google Business resources, most Google Play / App Store resources, Pinterest `url-stats`, and Amazon `product` run on a task-queue upstream. The API hides this behind a normal synchronous call, but expect **~10 to 45 seconds** of latency on those endpoints. Plan timeouts accordingly (60s is safe).

Separately, the web crawl / batch-scrape / agent endpoints are **async by design**: they return a `job_id` immediately, and you poll `GET /v1/web/jobs/{job_id}` or supply a `webhook_url`.

## Universal Search (`/v1/search/everywhere`)

Flat **20 credits** per call. Fans out across up to 17 sources in parallel (reddit, twitter-ai-search, youtube, tiktok, instagram, hackernews, polymarket, github, threads, pinterest, perplexity, tavily, linkedin, rumble + tiktok/instagram/youtube hashtag siblings in hashtag mode), then fuses, reranks, enriches with top comments, and clusters the results.

Two response modes via the `Accept` header:

- `application/json` (default): standard envelope with the full ranked result set.
- `text/event-stream`: typed SSE chunks: `meta`, `source_started`, `items`, `source_failed`, `plan_refined`, `ranked_partial`, `ranked_final`, `comments_enriched`, `clusters`, `warning`, `done`, `error`.

Fully refunded when every source fails or returns empty (sync and streaming both).

## Prism Composites (`/v1/prism/*`)

Server-side composites that fan out to several detail endpoints and fold the legs into one unified payload behind the standard envelope. Every composite emits a `legs[]` transparency array (`{endpoint, status, credits_used, latency_ms, error}`). Cross-platform recipes live under `/v1/prism/*`; a few keep their platform's own path and carry a `family: "prism"` flag (`{tiktok,instagram,youtube,twitter,facebook,linkedin}/profile/full`, `reddit/omni-search`). Pricing is flat or metered per recipe (0 to 50 credits); metered composites (e.g. `prism/comments`, `prism/ai-visibility`) deduct an upfront ceiling and refund to the actual work done. Streaming composites (`prism/comments`, `prism/answers`, `prism/profiles`, `prism/app-reviews`, `reddit/omni-search`) also support `Accept: text/event-stream`. Three composites are **POST** because their input is a list too large for a query string: `prism/post-stats`, `prism/profiles`, `prism/comment-lookup`. Full list: [prism.md](prism.md).

## Monitors (`/v1/monitors/*`)

A stateful, scheduled wrapper: a monitor re-runs any registered recipe or Prism composite on a cadence (hourly/daily/weekly/cron), delivers each result to an HMAC-signed webhook, evaluates alert rules, and accumulates a per-run time-series. Monitors are **not** registry endpoints (they sit outside the endpoint total) and use POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE. Managing them costs 0 credits; each scheduled run bills the recipe's normal cost plus a 1-credit scheduling premium. Full contract: [monitors.md](monitors.md).

## Platform Status

```bash
curl -s "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/status"
```

Returns per-platform circuit-breaker health. Each platform's breaker opens after 5 failures in 60s and stays open for 30s, during that window requests return `503` with `Retry-After: 30` and full refund.

## Error Codes

<!-- BEGIN:GENERATED:ERRORS (auto-generated by generate-docs.ts - AIP-16b) -->
| Code | Status | Retry? | What it means / what to do |
|------|--------|--------|----------------------------|
| MISSING_API_KEY | 401 | no | No x-api-key header on the request. Ask the user for their key and save it to `~/.config/socialcrawl/api_key` |
| INVALID_API_KEY | 401 | no | API key is malformed, not found, revoked, or expired. Tell the user to check the key at https://socialcrawl.dev/dashboard |
| INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS | 402 | no | Credit balance is lower than the endpoint cost. Point the user at https://socialcrawl.dev/dashboard/billing |
| INVALID_REQUEST | 400 | no | A required parameter is missing, a value failed validation, or no one-of group member was provided. Re-read the endpoint's params and Constraints in its platform reference before retrying - this is free, so a retry costs nothing |
| ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND | 404 | no | The platform or resource is not supported. Check the platform table, or call the free `GET /v1/utility/endpoints` to list the live surface |
| RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND | 404 | no | The requested item was not found on the platform; credits are refunded when triggered by an empty upstream result |
| CONCURRENCY_LIMIT | 429 | yes | More than 50 simultaneous requests on the same API key; honor Retry-After, then back off. Wait for the `Retry-After` value, then retry |
| UPSTREAM_ERROR | 502 | yes | The platform returned an error; credits are automatically refunded. Retry once, then report it as a platform-side outage |
| SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE | 503 | yes | Temporarily unavailable for this platform, either after repeated failures or because the upstream provider is rate-limiting us; honor Retry-After, credits are refunded. Retry after ~30s |
| INTERNAL_ERROR | 500 | yes | Unexpected server error; credits are automatically refunded |
| METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED | 405 | no | Wrong HTTP method for this endpoint. Check the method in the platform reference - the `/v1/web/*` job, monitor, and session routes and the batch endpoints are POST/PATCH/DELETE, not GET |
| IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT | 409 | no | The Idempotency-Key conflicts with an incompatible active reservation. Use a fresh Idempotency-Key |
| IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS | 409 | yes | A request with this Idempotency-Key is still running; retry after the Retry-After delay. Unbilled - wait for Retry-After, then retry with the same Idempotency-Key |
| IDEMPOTENCY_REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE | 409 | no | The original outcome is known, but its response body exceeded the idempotent replay storage limit; use a new key only to make a new billable request. The prior call already completed; use a new key only to make a new billable request |
| IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH | 422 | no | The Idempotency-Key was reused with a different request payload. Use a fresh Idempotency-Key for the changed payload |
| COHORT_MEMBER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED | 400 | no | The cohort member limit would be exceeded by this upload |
| COHORT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED | 400 | no | The account already holds the maximum number of cohorts |
| COHORT_IDENTITY_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED | 400 | no | The identity platform is not supported for cohort queries |
| COHORT_IDENTITY_CONFLICT | 409 | no | The normalized identity is already assigned to another external ID |
| COHORT_QUERY_NOT_CANCELLABLE | 409 | no | The cohort query is terminal and cannot be cancelled |
| COHORT_QUERY_NOT_READY | 409 | no | The cohort query has not completed and its results are not available |
| COHORT_RESULT_TOO_LARGE | 413 | no | One cohort query result exceeds the maximum response-page size |
| PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE | 413 | no | The JSON request body exceeds the 1 MB size limit |
| RATE_LIMITED | 429 | yes | More than 600 requests in a 1-minute window on the same API key; honor Retry-After, then back off. Unbilled - wait for `Retry-After`, then retry |
| KEY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED | 402 | no | This API key has spent its per-key credit limit; the account balance is unaffected. Raise or reset the key's limit in Dashboard → API Keys, or use a key with no limit |
<!-- END:GENERATED:ERRORS -->

Error envelopes include a `doc_url` pointing at `https://www.socialcrawl.dev/docs/errors/<code>`.
